verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The SWTBench harness reported FAILED with added_f2p 0 and coverage_pred 0.0, meaning the submitted tests never fail on base code and never flip to pass under the gold fix [1]. The task asked for test cases that verify a fix for stack casting an int32 coordinate to int64, and the MVCE explicitly compares values.dtype before and after stack [2]; the reference solution adds test_restore_dtype_on_multiindexes asserting str(foo["bar"].values.dtype) == dtype for int32 and float32 in test_indexes.py [3]. On the actual buggy base code, PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__ returns get_level_values(...).values without restoring the original dtype, so values.dtype becomes int64 while DataArray.dtype stays int32 [4]. The agent's final patch adds parametrized test_stack_retains_dtype in test_dataset.py and test_dataarray.py, but every assertion compares DataArray.dtype (e.g., ds["a"].dtype == ds.stack(c=("a",))["a"].dtype) rather than values.dtype [5], so those tests pass on unfixed code and cannot detect the reported bug. After reproducing the MVCE the agent saw True, concluded the issue was already fixed in the tree, and expanded tests without checking they would fail on the buggy behavior described in the issue [6][7]; its self-validation only ran the new tests locally and declared success when they passed [8]. Because the delivered tests are not valid fail-to-pass regression tests for the specified bug, the agent did not genuinely accomplish the task and TN is the right classification.
